subject.title: fix(agents): pass attemptNumber instead of apiKeyIndex to retry callbacks (#102938)

question: Should the public provider-auth retry callback permanently keep `attempt` as the supported key index while adding `apiKeyIndex` and `attemptNumber`, or should OpenClaw begin a formal deprecation lifecycle for `attempt`?
rationale: The helper is exported through the plugin SDK, so a deprecation is a public API lifecycle commitment that cannot be inferred from the bug fix alone.

options.title: Add fields, keep `attempt` supported
options.body: Remove the deprecation, retain current `attempt` semantics, and add the two explicit counters as a backward-compatible clarification.

options.title: Approve formal deprecation
options.body: Keep the annotation only with explicit maintainer approval, plugin-facing documentation, compatibility tests, and a named removal window.

options.title: Redesign the callback contract
options.body: Pause this PR and define a versioned or discriminated retry context if three overlapping counters are considered too ambiguous.

recommendation.title: Add fields, keep `attempt` supported
recommendation.body: Remove the deprecation, retain current `attempt` semantics, and add the two explicit counters as a backward-compatible clarification.

likelyOwner.reason: The original generic rotation API history and plugin-boundary ownership make this the strongest available routing candidate for the lifecycle choice.
